entry.code_revision: Author server jonpol01/d1a@aa35ec9928157bba999ccdcf1f4929403ebb0789, run unmodified using its native /v1/systemone endpoint and PyTorch BF16. JohnP1/d1a-e2b@42f61942442f06b9f4c572c071b63684f3ac0dea is an unmerged LoRA with adapter dimension 16 plus a fp32 pointer head and learned temperature on google/gemma-4-E2B@d29ff6b45f081a49ee2733a859c9c9c2d95d1a6f. No quantisation, vLLM or SGLang. The checkpoint's learned temperature and server defaults were used; feedback, learning, prefix cache, CUDA graphs, fused kernels, date facts and chat logging were disabled. No request use_case was injected. Dependencies were pinned and installed offline; author source and weights ran on isolated rented hardware with networking disabled.
entry.cost_basis: ESTIMATE (*est.), no base key, explicit labelled pair: the frozen pricing_v15 module (sha256 aa2afcd5a58d0c4cc0e3d6867d590c70b6ac58e971410c27faf9628f97bcf8b7, re-freeze of 22 Oct 2026) has no market-listing decision for the card's base string google/gemma-4-E2B (reference() raises 'base model lacks an explicit market-listing decision', checked on this module), and an explicit reference cannot rescue a declared base, so this row carries NO base_model key and names the real base here instead. SAME-FAMILY REFERENCE, ONE SIZE UP (self-hosted open weights, no bookable listing for this base). pricing_v15.reference() RAISES on google/gemma-4-E2B and on google/gemma-4-e2b - the base is in none of the three frozen tables - and the published page carries no exact-rate row on this base either (the Gemma-4-E2B entries on the board are system-one-open, listed not_measured, and classone-gemma4-e2b, which itself publishes at this same labelled pair). The row therefore carries its own labelled estimate from the nearest reference the frozen 25 Sep snapshot itself contains, deepinfra:google/gemma-4-E4B-it at USD 0.02 per 1M input and USD 0.10 per 1M output - the SAME Gemma-4 effective-parameter family, one size LARGER, so it is both the nearest available reference and the direction that cannot flatter this row - x this row's own measured tokens. Applied at USD 0.02 per 1M input and USD 0.10 per 1M output (the pair is explicit; deepinfra:google/gemma-4-E4B-it USD 0.02/M input, USD 0.1/M output). Estimated, not charged, not a quote from the author or any host. Tokens as reported natively by the usage block of the author's server: 1,648,992 input and 173,752 output tokens across all 1,500 answered items. Output tokens are NATIVE and NONZERO: the server reports the token count of the serialized answer it returns (a probability answer, no generated explanation), so the zero-output convention for native-probability rows is NOT applied and output is priced as reported at the full output rate. The native input unit counts header, state and question separately without a system turn or chat template, after the author's truncation; native input usage equals our first-party offline count exactly (0 mismatches over 1,500 items). The 15 items answered on a truncated prompt are INCLUDED in the usage and the cost at their truncated size. Arithmetic over all 1,500 rows: USD 0.033570 per 1,000 decisions = 0.52x the unchanged USD 0.06459465517241379 cap; the common 1,485-item basis figure is computed by the scorer. COST FIGURES: USD 0.020549 per 1,000 decisions on the common 1,485-item cost basis that the score uses (the same items for every token-priced row: all items except the 15 very long ones that the Jev reference refused); separately, USD 0.033570 per 1,000 decisions over all 1,500 rows of the draw. The common-basis figure is 0.32x the official cost cap USD 0.064595 (all-rows figure 0.52x).
entry.disclosure: First measurement of JohnP1/d1a-e2b, a Jev-compatible model. The native server returns probabilities for choice, noul and score using a pointer head, without text generation. Adapter and head hashes differ from the other measured Gemma 4 E2B/E4B siblings checked; byte distinctness does not establish independent training. The pinned card and training metadata describe general decisions, developer-tool tasks, long documents, Japanese JGLUE, routing and pull-request labels, with calibration fitted on decision-v7 calibration data and PR-label development data. These are author statements. Training examples and overlap with JevBench were not independently checked. Apache-2.0 is declared on the pinned cards and metadata; no standalone LICENSE file is present in the pinned model trees. The author's server truncates state to its first 65,536 tokens (including BOS and the state delimiter; a question row may use up to 73,728 tokens). Exactly 15 items were answered using a truncated prompt. All 1,500 requests returned HTTP 200 with probability answers; no refusals or errors occurred. Exactly those 15 truncated items exceeded 10 s (maximum 16.2 s); the v1.7 share view counts them as wrong answers with zero calibration. Frozen/off views have no time limit. Server-native input usage after truncation matched the independent tokenizer count on every request; native nonzero output usage counts the serialized probability answer and is priced as reported. Cost is an ESTIMATE, not charged usage or a host quote. The common cost basis excludes the same 15 long items for every row. Self-hosted latency uses the common assumption 2 times measured p50 plus 0.15 s. A 50-request repeat check had identical probabilities and zero argmax flips.
entry.endpoint_condition: Measured 26 Oct 2026 on one rented NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96 GB in Finland over loopback. The two models ran sequentially in fresh isolated containers with source, weights and inputs read-only, no credentials and networking disabled. GPU rental is separate from the estimated model tariff.
